llm_calls.rationale: DINOv2 is the only self-supervised encoder that consistently beats language-aligned models like CLIP on fine-grained vision tasks according to the evidence base, while EVA-02 and SigLIP are both bigger-but-different families that tend to lose on fine-grained tasks.

Both EVA-02 and SigLIP are bigger-but-different families that the evidence base shows tend to lose on fine-grained tasks, and since the move_class requires swapping to a different family than the current DINOv2 champion but no promising alternative families remain, no candidates are worth the sealed certification cost.
Fusion has never certified in any prior run and the evidence base shows it consistently dilutes performance on hard tasks, making this CLIP+DINOv2 concatenation not worth the sealed peek.
Within-family scaling from the winning DINOv2 family (300M→1.1B parameters) is the highest-probability improvement given that family changes don't help and scaling up has historically paid off.

note: Both runs use the frozen certifier as sole promoter and a shared memoized arena; only the proposal order/pruning differs. The strategist proposals are intersected with the policy's legal set, so the LLM can only reorder/prune -- never inject an illegal encoder or promote.
